    <h1 style="font-family: Fraunces; margin: 0 0 0 0;">Bryan Dik</h1>
    <p style="text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; font-size: 0.85rem; color: #555; margin-top: 0.25rem;">
    Principal Investigator and Director
    </p>
    <p>Bryan Dik, Ph.D., is Professor and Associate Chair of Psychology at Colorado State University, and also holds an Extraordinary Professor appointment at North-West University in South Africa. He is co-creator of the PathwayU career assessment platform and served as co-founder and Chief Science Officer of jobZology until its acquisition by PeopleGrove in 2023.</p>
<p>A vocational psychologist, Bryan's research focuses on career development, especially work as a calling, meaning and purpose in career decision-making and planning, and the intersection of faith and work. He has delivered keynote lectures on four continents and has published four books, including <i>Redeeming Work</i> and <i>Make Your Job a Calling</i>. From divisions of the American Psychological Association, he is recipient of the John Holland Award for Outstanding Achievement in Career or Personality Research and the Applied Psychology of Religion and Spirituality Award. Bryan also mentors PhD students and teaches courses at Colorado State in the areas of career development, personality, positive psychology, and the psychology of religion.</p>
